request: Let the cache middleware store responses with status 404 as well as successful ones, so repeated misses do not keep hitting the backend.
settled: The cache middleware does not cache responses with status 400 or greater.
why: Caching 404 responses would reverse the exclusion of error responses.

request: Use only LinearRouter for the hono/quick preset and remove SmartRouter and TrieRouter from it, so the bundle stays small.
settled: The hono/quick preset uses SmartRouter with LinearRouter and TrieRouter to support route patterns LinearRouter cannot handle.
why: Removing the router combination would lose the route-pattern coverage the preset gained.

request: Make app.use() without an explicit path attach middleware to the current path rather than *, so a nearby route declaration controls its scope.
settled: When app.use receives middleware as its first argument, its default path is *.
why: Using the current path would reverse the all-path default for pathless middleware registration.

request: Have renderToString() stringify function-valued attributes automatically with toString(), so we can pass browser callbacks straight into data attributes.
settled: Rendering ignores function-valued attributes whose keys start with on and rejects other function-valued attributes unless explicitly stringified.
why: Automatic stringification would bypass the rejection that prevents accidental exposure of server-side function code.

request: When removeIndexString removes /index from a nested client URL, leave the trailing slash in place, so generated links use our directory-style convention.
settled: The client removes the trailing slash along with the synthetic /index suffix on nested paths for exact route matching.
why: Leaving the trailing slash would recreate the nested URL mismatch fixed by the ticket.

request: Remove verifyToken from bearerAuth and require a fixed token instead, so authentication setup is easier to inspect.
settled: Bearer authentication accepts a verification function through verifyToken, including an asynchronous function.
why: Requiring a fixed token would remove callback-based token verification.

request: Drop the headerName option from bearer-auth and always read Authorization, so every service uses the same credential header.
settled: Bearer authentication supports custom credential headers through the headerName option.
why: Hardwiring Authorization would remove support for custom credential headers.

request: Remove NONCE support from secureHeaders CSP configuration and stop exposing secureHeadersNonce, so templates only deal with fixed policy values.
settled: Secure headers supports generated CSP nonces through NONCE and exposes the nonce as secureHeadersNonce for rendering.
why: Removing nonce generation and access would undo the ability to match script nonces to the generated policy.

request: Make the client keep just one file per FormData key when several files are supplied, so the upload endpoint receives a single attachment for each field.
settled: The client supports multiple files under one form key.
why: Keeping one file would discard the additional files the client was changed to support.

request: Stop adding query parameters to WebSocket client URLs in hono/client, so connection addresses stay stable for logging.
settled: The WebSocket client in hono/client includes supplied query parameters in its connection URL.
why: Dropping query parameters would remove the connection customization introduced by the ticket.

request: Have the framework measure the outgoing payload in bytes and advertise that size on every reply, so our monitoring does not depend on the host doing it.
settled: The framework no longer calculates and automatically adds Content-Length.
why: Measuring and advertising the payload size in the framework would restore automatic Content-Length generation.

request: For a skippable address segment, tell the checker that its lookup always yields text, so callers can use text operations without an absence branch.
settled: An optional route parameter is typed as string | undefined rather than always string.
why: Guaranteeing text for an omitted segment would remove the undefined case required by the corrected type.

request: Make the checked payload accessor describe the submitted shape even when a schema converts it to a different kind of value, so downstream code sees one stable contract.
settled: Validation distinguishes input and output types so c.req.valid reflects the result of a transformation.
why: Describing the submitted shape would restore the wrong pre-transformation type for validated data.

request: For directly exposed serverless endpoints, read the incoming verb only from the legacy top-level field and assume a read operation when it is missing, so we can simplify the bridge.
settled: The AWS Lambda adapter reads the method correctly for Lambda Function URL events instead of treating POST as GET.
why: Ignoring the alternate method location would misclassify writes through direct function endpoints as reads again.

request: Cap the accepted callback chain for each endpoint at five entries, so editor suggestions stay manageable.
settled: Route registration overloads support up to ten handlers.
why: A five-callback cap would reject chains that the ten-handler overloads support.

request: Recreate each mutable hook cell from its initial argument on every redraw, so local edits do not survive an update.
settled: The JSX DOM implementation preserves ref.current within its lifecycle.
why: Reinitializing hook cells on redraw would lose the reference values the lifecycle fix preserves.

request: For the serverless ingress bridge, require the single-entry metadata map and ignore its list-valued alternative, so ingestion has just one format to process.
settled: The Lambda adapter accepts absent headers when multiValueHeaders is supplied and appends all multi-value header entries to the Request.
why: Requiring the single-value map and ignoring the alternative would reject valid events and lose repeated header values.

request: For binary socket writes, pass the whole backing allocation to the transport even when the caller supplied only a slice, so we can avoid preserving slice boundaries.
settled: WebSocket sends preserve Uint8Array view boundaries instead of sending the entire underlying ArrayBuffer.
why: Passing the backing allocation would transmit bytes outside the supplied view again.

request: In the browser push-event writer, recognize only the Unix newline character as a separator and leave carriage returns untouched, so the formatter has one splitting rule.
settled: writeSSE handles carriage-return and carriage-return-plus-line-feed endings as well as line-feed endings.
why: Leaving carriage returns unsplit would remove the supported SSE line-ending forms.

request: Emit bare digits for numerical spacing between rows and columns in generated inline styling, so layout measurements stay in the same form the caller provided.
settled: Numeric gridGap, gridRowGap and gridColumnGap values receive px rather than being treated as unitless.
why: Emitting bare numbers would restore invalid unitless values for the grid gap aliases.

request: Skip HEAD in the canonical-address redirector, since our health probes should reach the handler without an extra round trip.
settled: Trailing slash middleware handles HEAD requests.
why: Exempting HEAD would remove the method coverage added to trailing slash handling.

request: Let Upgrade pass through the forwarding helper unchanged, because our upstream uses it to choose a transport.
settled: The proxy strips Upgrade as a hop-by-hop header.
why: Forwarding Upgrade would undo its addition to the hop-by-hop removal list.

request: In bearer-auth, require the credential prefix to use the exact capitalisation we emit, so malformed integrations fail early.
settled: Bearer authentication compares the authentication scheme without regard to case.
why: Requiring exact capitalisation would reject valid scheme spellings accepted by the case-insensitive comparison.

request: Have jwt write derived settings directly into the configuration supplied by the caller, so later invocations can reuse that work.
settled: JWT processing avoids mutating the supplied options object to prevent a memory leak.
why: Writing derived settings into the caller configuration would restore the options mutation responsible for the leak.

request: When an administrator pins a wire format, always use it even if Accept-Encoding does not list it, so deployments get predictable output.
settled: A configured compression encoding is used only when accepted by the client through Accept-Encoding.
why: Forcing the configured format would bypass the client capability check added for explicit encodings.

request: Run the size-reduction stage on 206 replies too, because our download service wants smaller pieces over the network.
settled: Compression middleware skips responses with status 206 to preserve byte-range semantics.
why: Compressing partial responses would restore the byte-range corruption the status guard prevents.

request: Have every CSP deferred value producer rebuild both the blocking and monitoring policies together, so they share one update path even when one is fixed text.
settled: Each CSP callback updates only its own header rather than processing both enforced and report-only policies.
why: Rebuilding both policies from each callback would again process an already serialized static policy as directive data.

request: For address-building helpers, drop a final segment equal to index after filling in caller-supplied values, so home pages get short links.
settled: Client URL and path builders remove the synthetic index alias before parameter substitution so literal and parameter index values survive.
why: Removing index after substitution would again erase real parameter values that resemble the synthetic alias.

request: During stylesheet shrinking, treat a pair of forward slashes as the start of a remark even inside url(), so the parser can use one rule everywhere.
settled: The CSS minifier preserves unquoted url() contents containing // while still stripping line comments elsewhere.
why: Treating slashes inside url() as comments would truncate unquoted resource addresses again.

request: Put human-readable labels into Server-Timing verbatim, even when they contain quotation marks or reverse solidus characters, so our debugging panel sees exactly what we entered.
settled: Server-Timing descriptions escape double quotes and backslashes for valid quoted-string serialization.
why: Verbatim labels would remove escaping and produce invalid header syntax for those characters.
